items.cite: Philip Glass, *Words Without Music: A Memoir* (Liveright, 2015).
items.note: The composer’s own account of the Baltimore record shop, the lessons with Boulanger, the travels in India and Central Asia and the day jobs of the 1960s and 1970s.

items.cite: Philip Glass, *Music by Philip Glass*, edited by Robert T. Jones (Harper & Row, 1987; Da Capo Press, 1995).
items.note: Glass on his early pieces and the portrait operas; Tim Page’s notes for the Nonesuch recordings quote it on Einstein.

items.cite: Keith Potter, *Four Musical Minimalists: La Monte Young, Terry Riley, Steve Reich, Philip Glass* (Cambridge University Press, 2000).
items.note: Treats Glass together with La Monte Young, Terry Riley and Steve Reich, and places his early work among his New York contemporaries.

items.cite: Tim Page, ‘“Einstein on the Beach”—Philip Glass, Robert Wilson (1979)’, essay for the Library of Congress National Recording Registry (2012).
items.note: How Glass and Wilson chose their subject, what the text and music consist of, and how the 1976 performances were received.

items.cite: Alex Ross, ‘Sound and Vision’, *The New Yorker*, 27 June 2005.
items.note: A review of the Lincoln Center performances of the three Reggio films, with an account of how the score for Koyaanisqatsi was fitted to the images.
